title: Admin approval workflow and admin removal of published articles (frontend-only)

requirements.summary: Ensure user submissions remain pending until admin publishes, and keep public pages showing only published stories.
acceptanceCriteria: A story submitted via the existing submission flow is not returned by any public endpoint used by the feed/articles pages until an admin publishes it.
The admin-only publish action is required to make a submission publicly visible.
User-facing copy related to this flow remains in English.

file_operations.description: Align admin hooks with the current backend interface by (1) fetching pending submissions via the backend capability for pending stories and (2) publishing a pending submission via the backend capability for admin publish. Also add an admin-check query (e.g., using the backend capability that returns whether the caller is admin) to support admin-only UI gating. Use the selected "authorization" component concepts (role-based access control) to drive admin gating logic; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Update the moderation UI to use the revised admin hooks: show only pending submissions in the moderation list, and publish a selected pending story using the backend publish capability. Remove/adjust any UI that depends on non-existent reword-and-publish or all-stories fetching. Add an explicit admin-only guard using the admin-check query and show the existing AccessDeniedState when unauthorized (per the selected "authorization" component guidance); verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Keep submission confirmation messaging explicitly stating the story will be reviewed and is not publicly visible until published (English-only copy). Ensure the page continues to guide users to My Submissions for status tracking after submission.

Ensure the pending vs published status presentation remains clear and consistent with the approval workflow (pending submissions should not offer public viewing). Keep all user-facing status copy in English.

requirements.summary: Provide admin-only UI to view published articles and remove/unpublish them, updating React Query caches and showing not-found after removal.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes an admin-only method to remove a published story by title, and it rejects non-admin callers with an Unauthorized error.
Admin UI provides a way to view published articles and remove one by selecting it and confirming removal.
After removal, the deleted article no longer appears on the Articles page or Feed page, and navigating to its detail route shows a not-found/error state.
React Query caches for published stories are invalidated after removal so the UI updates without a hard refresh.

file_operations.description: Add an admin-only removal mutation that calls the backend capability to delete a published article by title. On success, invalidate React Query caches for the published stories list and the per-title published story query so Articles/Feed and detail views update without refresh. Incorporate admin gating/error handling consistent with the selected "authorization" component (Unauthorized traps should surface as a controlled UI state); verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Extend the admin moderation view with a published-articles section (e.g., an additional tab) that lists published stories and allows the admin to remove one by selecting it and confirming (e.g., via a confirmation prompt). After removal, ensure the list refreshes via cache invalidation and the removed item is no longer shown. Keep admin-only access guarded using the admin-check flow aligned with the selected "authorization" component; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Ensure the Articles page reliably reflects removals by depending on the existing published-stories query and rendering appropriate empty/error states after cache invalidation. No admin controls should appear here (admin removal stays within admin UI).
Ensure the Feed page reliably reflects removals by depending on the existing published-stories query and rendering appropriate empty/error states after cache invalidation.
Confirm that when the published story query fails (e.g., after admin removal), the page shows a clear not-found/error state and a way back to the Articles page.
Confirm that when the published story query fails (e.g., after admin removal), the page shows a clear not-found/error state and a way back to the Feed page.
